content:
If you have been testing beta versions of Apple Watch apps this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is pushing automatic updates on behalf of developers.

The update is rolling out via the App Store, with release notes stating: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features are included."

Apple notified developers earlier this week that the entire update process would be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, iOS 27, and other new operating systems are expected to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates should be completed before the public launch.

Apple explained that the measure is necessary because some watchOS apps are experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture. Reports indicate that the company is automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without requiring additional action from developers.
